title: Getting Started with the Self-Control-Risk-Interval (SCRI) Analysis Package
text: Self-Control-Risk-Interval (SCRI) R package provides pipeline apply Self-Controlled Risk Interval (SCRI) analysis modular reproducible format. vignette focuses vaccine safety setting aligned package manuscript introduction. study question whether risk acute events special interest increases COVID-19 vaccination compared control periods within person. worked example: - Exposure anchors covid_vaccine_1 covid_vaccine_2 - Outcomes interest myocarditis pericarditis - Censoring applied using death_date general_end_fup

title: Getting Started with the Self-Control-Risk-Interval (SCRI) Analysis Package
text: can install development version package GitHub:
code: # install.packages("devtools") library(devtools) devtools::install_github("UMC-Utrecht-RWE/SCRI")

title: Getting Started with the Self-Control-Risk-Interval (SCRI) Analysis Package
text: SCRI package workflow follows: Prepare input data: Study population, window metadata, records tables. Construct analysis windows: Define risk, control, windows subject. Apply censoring/cleaning rules: Trim windows based follow-censoring criteria. Match events windows: Identify outcomes/events window. Prepare analysis dataset: Summarize events person-time. Run analysis: Fit conditional logistic regression models. Summarize interpret results.

title: Getting Started with the Self-Control-Risk-Interval (SCRI) Analysis Package
text: package provides four example datasets needed run SCRI analysis: 1. StudyPopulation: Subject-level data reference dates (e.g., prescription dates) follow-boundaries 2. WindowMetadata: Definitions analysis windows (risk, control, washout, etc.) durations timing relative reference dates 3. RecordsTable: Outcome events (e.g., adverse events, hospitalizations) dates subject 4. WindowPriority: Priority rules defining window takes precedence windows consecutive doses overlap
code: data("StudyPopulation") DT::datatable(StudyPopulation, options = list(scrollX = TRUE)) data("WindowMetadata") DT::datatable(WindowMetadata, options = list(scrollX = TRUE)) data("RecordsTable") DT::datatable(RecordsTable, options = list(scrollX = TRUE)) data("WindowPriority") DT::datatable(WindowPriority, options = list(scrollX = TRUE))

title: Getting Started with the Self-Control-Risk-Interval (SCRI) Analysis Package
text: Calculate start end dates analysis window. output one row per dose/reference date, t0_date column used later order consecutive doses. happens: - person (id) reference date (covid_vaccine_1, covid_vaccine_2), windows computed relative date - t0_date set equal reference date used downstream order doses chronologically - Window definitions WindowMetadata (e.g., risk, control, washout) applied - row contains start_ end_ columns every window type Output structure: row represents one subject-dose combination. subject 2 reference dates (covid_vaccine_1 covid_vaccine_2), 2 rows per subject. Columns include id, t0_date, start_/end_ pairs window (e.g., start_risk, end_risk, start_control, end_control).
code: # Construct windows for all subjects relative to their covid_vaccine_1 and covid_vaccine_2 dates constructed_windows <- construct_window(     study_population = StudyPopulation, # Input: subject characteristics and reference dates     window_metadata = WindowMetadata, # Input: window definitions (duration, lag, etc.)     reference_date_name = c("covid_vaccine_1", "covid_vaccine_2"), # Dates to anchor windows around     id_column = "id" # Column identifying each subject )  # Display first few rows with all computed window dates DT::datatable(head(constructed_windows), options = list(scrollX = TRUE))

title: Getting Started with the Self-Control-Risk-Interval (SCRI) Analysis Package
text: Apply censoring rules (e.g., end follow-death) overlap-priority rules consecutive doses ordered t0_date. happens: 1. Censoring: person dies reaches end--follow-, window end dates censoring date trimmed censoring date 2. Overlap resolution: person multiple doses (e.g., two prescriptions), windows dose N dose N+1 may overlap. Priority rules define dose’s window takes precedence: - Priority “”: Dose N window prevails → dose N+1 window start shifted forward - Priority “B”: Dose N+1 window prevails → dose N window end trimmed backward priority rules define possible combinations window types. Within cell, “” represents priority dose_n dose_n_plus_1 “B” represents opposite. Output changes: - Window end dates clamped censoring dates applicable - subjects multiple doses, overlapping windows resolved per priority rules - Window dates may now NAs fall entirely censoring event
code: # Display priority rules: which window takes precedence in overlaps DT::datatable(WindowPriority, options = list(scrollX = TRUE)) # Apply censoring and overlap-priority rules to clean the windows wrangled_windows <- wrangle_window(     constructed_windows, # Input: windows from Step 1     censoring_dates = c("death_date", "general_end_fup"), # Trim windows at these dates     windows_priority = WindowPriority # Apply priority rules for N vs N+1 overlaps )  # Display cleaned windows (dates may be trimmed or shifted compared to constructed_windows) DT::datatable(wrangled_windows, options = list(scrollX = TRUE))

title: Getting Started with the Self-Control-Risk-Interval (SCRI) Analysis Package
text: Identify outcomes/events occurred within window. happens: - record (outcome event) RecordsTable matched windows wrangled_windows - record’s date falls within window’s start end dates, flagged occurring window - add_records() function creates indicators window showing whether outcome occurred - Option: Keep first event per person, retain events Output structure: - Original window columns retained - New indicator columns show presence/absence events window - stratification needed, columns also present - Rows without matching records may retained (useful “unexposed” person-windows)
code: # Match each outcome event to the appropriate window(s) identified_records <- add_records(     window_data = wrangled_windows, # Input: cleaned windows with adjusted dates     records = RecordsTable, # Input: outcome events with dates     only_first_record = TRUE # TRUE: keep only first event per subject; FALSE: keep all )  # Display records with window assignments (new columns indicate which window each event occurred in) DT::datatable(identified_records, options = list(scrollX = TRUE))

title: Getting Started with the Self-Control-Risk-Interval (SCRI) Analysis Package
text: Summarize events person-time per window analysis. happens: - Event counts person-time aggregated window, outcome type, (optionally) stratification variables - Outcome indicators rolled : event occurred window, person-window marked outcome - Person-time calculated number days window (end_date - start_date) - dataset restructured match format required conditional logistic regression Output structure: - Rows represent person-window-outcome combinations - Columns include window identifiers, outcome status (1/0), person-time, stratification variables - format ready conditional logistic regression - subject appears per window type (e.g., risk window, control window)
code: # Aggregate to create analytical dataset with events and person-time analytical_dataset <- prepare_analytical_dataset(     SCRI_identified_records = identified_records, # Input: records matched to windows     strata_column_name = NULL, # Optional: column for stratification (or NULL for no stratification)     only_first_date = TRUE # TRUE: use only first occurrence per person; FALSE: use all )  # Display analytical dataset (one row per person-window combination) DT::datatable(analytical_dataset, options = list(scrollX = TRUE))

title: Getting Started with the Self-Control-Risk-Interval (SCRI) Analysis Package
text: Apply statistical model estimate exposure effects. happens: - conditional logistic regression fit event status (outcome/outcome) dependent variable - model conditions subject account person-level confounding (self-controlled design) - reference window (e.g., “control”) defines unexposed person-time - Risk windows define exposure periods - model compares odds outcome risk window vs. control window, within person Output structure: - Columns include parameter estimates, odds ratios (ORs), confidence intervals (CIs), p-values - One row per window comparison (e.g., “risk” vs. reference window) - ORs > 1 indicate increased risk window; ORs < 1 indicate decreased risk - Statistical significance determined whether CI excludes 1.0
code: # Fit conditional logistic regression comparing windows within persons results <- apply_analysis(     SCRI_analytical_dataset = analytical_dataset, # Input: aggregated analytical dataset     reference_date_name = "covid_vaccine_1", # Which reference date to use     reference_window = "risk", # Which window serves as the baseline (usually "control")     strata_column_name = NULL # Optional: column for stratified analysis ) #> [1] "[SCRI] No events in control or risk windows for myocarditis" #> [1] "[SCRI] No events in induction or risk windows for myocarditis" #> [1] "[SCRI] No events in washout or risk windows for myocarditis" #> [1] "[SCRI] for control vs risk model, pericarditis model fit returns could not find function \"strata\"" #> [1] "[SCRI] for induction vs risk model, pericarditis model fit returns could not find function \"strata\"" #> [1] "[SCRI] for washout vs risk model, pericarditis model fit returns could not find function \"strata\""  # Display results (odds ratios, confidence intervals, p-values) DT::datatable(results, options = list(scrollX = TRUE))

title: Getting Started with the Self-Control-Risk-Interval (SCRI) Analysis Package
text: can use main scri() function run entire pipeline end--end single call. : - Internally performs 5 steps (construct → clean → match → prepare → analyze) - Useful quick analyses don’t need intermediate outputs - Less flexible stepwise approach, concise Advantages: - Single function call replaces 5 separate steps - Automatically handles data flow functions - internal steps use validation error checking Disadvantages: - inspect intermediate outputs (windows /cleaning, records matching) - Less flexibility custom processing steps
code: # Run complete SCRI analysis in one function call final_results <- SCRI::scri(     study_population = StudyPopulation, # Subject data with reference dates     window_metadata = WindowMetadata, # Window definitions     window_priority = WindowPriority, # Priority rules for dose overlaps     records_table = RecordsTable, # Outcome events     reference_date_name = "covid_vaccine_1", # Which reference date to use     reference_window = "control", # Baseline window for comparison     start_followup_criteria = "op_start_date", # Window construction start point     end_followup_criteria = c("death_date", "general_end_fup"), # Censoring dates     only_first_date = TRUE # Keep only first event per person ) #> [1] "[SCRI] No events in induction or control windows for myocarditis" #> [1] "[SCRI] No events in risk or control windows for myocarditis" #> [1] "[SCRI] No events in washout or control windows for myocarditis" #> [1] "[SCRI] for induction vs control model, pericarditis model fit returns could not find function \"strata\"" #> [1] "[SCRI] for risk vs control model, pericarditis model fit returns could not find function \"strata\"" #> [1] "[SCRI] for washout vs control model, pericarditis model fit returns could not find function \"strata\""  # Display final analysis results DT::datatable(final_results, options = list(scrollX = TRUE))

title: Getting Started with the Self-Control-Risk-Interval (SCRI) Analysis Package
text: can query available self-controlled designs valid models:
code: get_ValidModels() #>   model_name                                                        description #> 1    log_reg   Logistic regression: used for modeling binary outcome variables. #> 2    lin_reg Linear regression: used for modeling continuous outcome variables.

title: Getting Started with the Self-Control-Risk-Interval (SCRI) Analysis Package
text: SCRI pipeline highly customizable multiple levels: Edit WindowMetadata change risk/control period durations, lags, structure Example: Extend washout period 7 14 days modifying duration lag columns Modify WindowPriority define overlaps consecutive doses resolved Example: Switch priority “” ↔︎ “B” give dose N+1 precedence instead dose N Add stratification columns StudyPopulation (e.g., age group, sex) Specify column name SCRI() apply_analysis() run separate models per stratum Use date column StudyPopulation (e.g., “death_date”, “end_of_followup”, “emigration_date”) Specify multiple censoring columns; windows trimmed earliest censoring event Advanced: Use apply_timevarying() include covariates change follow-Note: Experimental feature, consult documentation details Set only_first_date = TRUE analyze first outcome occurrence Set only_first_date = FALSE analyze occurrences

title: Getting Started with the Self-Control-Risk-Interval (SCRI) Analysis Package
text: SCRI package provides comprehensive, modular, reproducible workflow conducting self-controlled risk interval analysis: Flexible design: Choose stepwise control (5 individual steps) --one pipeline, depending needs Customizable: Adapt windows, priorities, censoring, stratification study design Transparent: step produces interpretable outputs suitable sensitivity analyses validation Self-controlled framework: Automatically accounts time-invariant confounding matched analysis design information, advanced usage, troubleshooting, please see: - Package documentation: ?SCRI individual function help pages - GitHub repository: UMC-Utrecht-RWE/SCRI - Published methods paper: [Reference applicable]

what: SCRI: Self-Controlled Risk Interval analysis for repeated exposures
title: Self Controlled Risk Interval Analysis
text: SCRI R package performing Self-Controlled Risk Interval (SCRI) analyses. supports flexible study designs multiple reference dates, repeated exposures doses, configurable risk-window priorities. package provides end--end workflow : - validating study inputs window definitions, - constructing analysis windows exposure reference dates, - resolving overlapping censored windows, - matching outcome records analysis windows, - preparing analytical datasets, - estimating event counts, person-time, incidence rate ratios, confidence intervals using conditional logistic regression.
